content.introduction: The next key support level for the stock market comes in around 7,300, which represents the 200-day Simple Moving Average (SMA) and coincides with the July 29th close at 7,316. The breadth of the SPX improved to 51.07% from 47.98%. The Chicago PMI came in at 55.3, down from the prior reading of 58.8 and below the 57.2 economists were expecting, but still in expansionary territory. EIA Crude Oil Inventories decreased by 1.892 million barrels, and EIA Natural Gas Inventories increased by 80 billion cubic feet.
body:
coming weeks, the next key support level comes in around 7,300, which roughly represents the 200-day Simple Moving Average (SMA) and coincides with the July 29th close at 7,316. [...] line) improved to 51.07% from 47.98%. [...] Chicago PMI: Came in at 55.3, which is down from the prior reading of 58.8 and below the 57.2 economists were expecting, but still in expansionary territory (above the 50.0 threshold).
   EIA Crude Oil Inventories: -1.892M barrels.
   EIA Natural Gas Inventories: +80 bcf.

If you read last Friday's blog, you might recall that I had a "breakout" outlook for stocks this week, noting that the S&P 500 Index (SPX) and Philadelphia Semiconductor Index (SOX) were at key intermediate-term support levels, which I felt set them up for an outsized weekly move (either higher or lower). There was a "bounce attempt" in stocks in the first half of this week (the Nasdaq was up 2% on the week by Wednesday's close) but then encountered a strong sell-off on Thursday, with some [...] Next week we'll get the monthly Personal Consumption Expenditures (PCE) Prices report, which has the potential to introduce some market volatility (recall: Consumer Price Index, or CPI and Producer Price Index, or PPI were warm/hot), and of course there will be a Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) meeting (a surprise is always possible, but expectations for a rate hike are very low) but the key driver will likely be the earnings reports from Alphabet, Amazon, and Microsoft on [...] April. Compared to last week, the SPX (white line) breadth moved up to 60.12% from 54.60%, the CCMP (blue line) fell to 36.61% from 36.59%, and the RUT (red line) dropped to 47.98% from 45.87%.
